subject: SLA thresholds, credit mechanics, and temporary exception plan
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudvertex.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@cloudvertex.com
Date: 2026-10-24T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template review — initial asks

Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking through Redwood's hosted proposal earlier. We reviewed the SLA draft with engineering and finance. Two items we need clarity on before we proceed:

1) Uptime baseline: CVX prefers a 99.98% monthly uptime for the customer-critical inference endpoints. Your draft lists 99.95% as the standard.
2) Remedy mechanics: Finance needs a deterministic monthly credit calculation rather than a discretionary "up to" percent of monthly fees.

Practical ask: can you propose a short-term concession for the first three months of the pilot where we accept 99.95% but have a fixed credit schedule if availability drops (so we can reconcile invoicing quickly)? After pilot, we'd like to migrate to 99.98% with the standard percent-of-bill credits.

Also, engineering flagged maintenance windows and burst processing as likely causes of transient P95 latency spikes — can those be explicitly carved out or subject to a different latency SLO?

Attached: a one-page summary of our requirements (cvx-remedy-exhibit.docx).

Best,
Amit
Contracts & Procurement — CloudVertex
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudvertex.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template review — initial asks

Amit,

Thanks — and appreciate the clear asks. We're aligned on the goal: predictable economics during the pilot, and stronger commitments post-pilot. Below is a concrete proposal from Redwood that we think balances predictability and platform operational realities. Please let us know if this is acceptable as a starting point and we'll produce an updated draft SLA (v3).

Summary proposal (pilot period = first 90 days after go-live):
- Uptime baseline: 99.95% (pilot).
- Fixed monthly credit schedule during pilot (deterministic, not discretionary):
  * 99.95% - 99.90%: 5% credit of that month's Redwood invoice (applies to the invoice covering the affected month).
  * 99.90% - 99.00%: 15% credit.
  * < 99.00%: 50% credit capped at a flat-dollar ceiling equal to one month of committed fees.
- Credit cap: pilot credits capped at 50% of monthly committed fees.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (published 7 days in advance and limited to 4 hours per calendar month per region) will be excluded from uptime calculations. Unscheduled maintenance will be treated as availability events unless we provide a post-mortem within 72 hours showing clear operational cause.
- Latency: we propose a separate p95 latency SLO for customer-critical endpoints at 300ms for the pilot. Burst processing and cold-starts tied to scaling events will be excluded from latency SLO coverage for the first 30 days post-scale event.

Next steps we propose:
1) If acceptable, Redwood will: (a) produce SLA v3 with the pilot credit table and carveouts, and (b) attach a Maintenance Calendar (we can align windows with CVX regions).
2) Ben (copied) will follow up on commercial points for the committed-fees cap.
3) Rishi will run a quick legal pass on the remedy wording for the fixed credit table.

I attached our current draft (redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf) and a maintenance calendar template. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Director — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf, maintenance-calendar.csv
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudvertex.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-25T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template review — initial asks

Amit —

Quick commercial note from our side: the pilot credit cap Kimberly proposed (50% of monthly committed fees) is intended to provide a bright-line protection for both parties. If CloudVertex prefers a deterministic dollar-based cap instead of a percentage, we can translate it — roughly speaking, 50% of your committed pilot spend (per the deal summary) maps to $38,500/month.

Options we can take to the contract:
- Keep the percentage table (simpler for both sides).
- Replace the cap line with an explicit dollar cap (CVX requested approach).

If you confirm the preferred method, I'll update the commercial exhibit and include it in SLA v3.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudvertex.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@cloudvertex.com
Date: 2026-10-26T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template review — initial asks

Ben / Kimberly,

Thanks — that helps. CVX prefers an explicit dollar cap for the pilot so our FP&A can reconcile quickly. If $38,500/month is the equivalent you mentioned, that works for us as the cap during the 90-day pilot.

Couple of follow-ups from engineering:
- Maintenance windows: CVX requests at least 48 hours' notice for any regional maintenance that will affect inference endpoints. Can we move to a 48-hour SLA for publishing scheduled maintenance notices?
- Latency carveouts: engineering accepts the 30-day post-scale carveout if Redwood commits to an operational dashboard feed that shows scaling events and cold-start counts. Is there an API we can pull?

If we can get those two items in writing (48-hour notice + scaling telemetry feed), CVX is happy to accept the pilot numbers and move forward. Please attach the updated SLA and a one-page exhibit with the $ cap and maintenance cadence.

Regards,
Amit
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudvertex.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template review — initial asks

Amit —

Appreciate the fast turn. We can commit to both asks for the pilot:
- Publication cadence: Redwood will publish scheduled maintenance notices at least 48 hours in advance for any maintenance that could impact inference endpoints in a region. We will maintain the maintenance-calendar.csv (attached) and update it in Drive.
- Telemetry feed: Redwood will provide a read-only scaling/ops events API endpoint and a dashboard link for CVX. The feed will include timestamps for scale events, instance counts, and cold-start flags for the affected endpoints. We'll include the API URL in SLA v3 (read-only key to be provisioned on go-live).

Action items we will complete today:
1) SLA v3 (redwood-sla-draft-v3.pdf) with the pilot credit table and explicit $38,500/month cap.
2) Commercial exhibit (pilot-credit-exhibit.pdf) with the dollar cap and the 3-month pilot timeframe.
3) Ops feed doc and temporary read-only key process (ops-feed-readme.md).

Ben and Rishi will run the commercial/legal edits and send final redlines by Friday. If you want to shortcut, I'm available for a 20-minute alignment call this afternoon.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Director — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (updated to be replaced by v3), maintenance-calendar.csv
